recipes.name: Egg and Spinach Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and drained
1 (16 ounce) package small curd cottage cheese

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

Beat eggs, onion, and flour in a mixing bowl until flour is no longer lumpy. Stir in spinach, cottage cheese, Cheddar cheese, butter, salt, and pepper until evenly combined; pour into the prepared dish.
Bake casserole in the preheated oven until bubbly and golden brown, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Egg and Spinach Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This quick spinach, egg, and cottage cheese casserole is ready in just 1 hour.

review.reviewBody: Added two extra eggs to stretch the meal. Not enough spinach, added more (mine was fresh steamed), plus 1/4 cup fresh parsley and full cup of chopped onion. Had some feta so I threw in a crumbled handful. Added lots of spice - generous paprika and chili powder, plus 1/4 tsp garlic powder, basil, black pepper, and a little salt. Left the butter out. I will use this recipe again with the changes noted!

Recipe was a hit! Next time I think I'll add the 2 extra eggs, more onion, and cheese on top as well. With 6 eggs I'd probably check it after 35-40mins. Mushrooms and tomatoes added would be really good! It'd also be good served with taco sauce or sauce baked on top. These were my changes: 3/4c diced red onion sauteed in 1T butter, no other butter. ~3/4c fluffed ricotta cheese instead of cottage cheese. ~2 1/4c shredded cheddar cheese. White pepper instead. ~2 1/2c de-stemmed fresh spinach leaves, torn up when added to mix. -Beat eggs, mix in flour until not lumpy, mix in sauteed red onion, blend in ricotta until smooth, mix in shredded cheddar, mix in salt and white pepper, blend in spinach leaves tearing up as added.

Cleaning out the fridge so used ricotta instead of cottage cheese and added a package of mushrooms. Yum
Omitted the butter, sautéed the mushrooms and onions first, and used 8 eggs

I will definitely make this again. It's a great template as you can add whatever you have on hand. 

As per other reviewers, next time I will omit the butter to save on calories (even though it turned out fine with it). 

I did a half batch and cooked it in a muffin pan making 6 single serving size 'muffins'. I used sautéed green pepper, green onion, and onion for 4 of the 'muffins' and then added spinach to the remaining 2.

This is great and pretty simple! I'm glad I read the reviews - the butter definitely is not needed; I made some other slight changes - used 12 oz cottage cheese and 8 oz cheddar. Also used fresh spinach which I sautéed with the onion and some red bell pepper. Easy to modify for personal taste or ingredients on hand. I really liked the texture too - a keeper!

I sauteed the onions first, added two extra eggs, and substituted with some ricotta since I didn't have enough cottage cheese. I also added some garlic powder and left out the butter. This recipe is good enough to stand on its own, but easy to modify, too. I took it to a breakfast event and it was very quickly eaten. Thank you!

A nice base recipe. You can add more veg, different cheeses. I sautee the spinach in a little butter (like a tsp) and do not add any more butter. I put the onion and some garlic as I sautee the spinach. I leave out the flour. Like others, I use 8 eggs total.

Great base recipe... I used egg substitute & added 2 extra eggs. added 2 sections of shallots in addition to the onion/ shallot & sautéed with 1/2 chopped each zucchini and yellow squash and 1/2 c. crumbled bacon which I sautéed with the fresh spinach and a bit of EVOO. I substituted sharp Irish cheddar.

This was fantastic. I've made it twice now - both in a muffin pan for individual servings. I used 1/: the butter the second time and Monterey/cheddar mix cheese. The first time I used Swiss Guyere mix (which was SO good with the spinach). I think mix of cheese is up to preference. I also added a teaspoon of dried Thyme and no need for any extra salt. A fantastic recipe!!!

This is a great recipe. I sautéed the onions with some garlic, and then wilted 16oz of fresh spinach in there. Let it cool and chopped the spinach. I also added 1lb of crumbled bacon and a few extra eggs and skipped the butter. This was a huge hit at my brunch. I even made it the day before and then just reheated.
Substitute Gluten-free flour and my family member never knew it was knew it was Gluten-free. So easy to make.
Really yummy. I used 3 eggs, half the cheese and a little garlic powder. Served at Thanksgiving and it was a hit!

I have made this several times. My family loves it, and coworkers have asked me for the recipe. I like to add Italian Seasoning. Also, I add a cooked meat; such as ground pork or bacon. Today I added mushrooms.
Our family loved this - I was able to make it gluten free by doing a substitution of the same amount of cup-for-cup gluten-free flour (I used King Arthur brand).
A family favorite!!!! We love spinach, so we double that. Awesome recipe!!
I loved it and the rest of my family liked it. Added more spices. Cooked the onions before adding them. Halved the cheese for Lactose intolerant daughter.
This was absolutely delicious. I used twice as much spinach and half the cheddar cheese. I liked this so much, I think this will be our Thanksgiving vegetarian entree.

Very good. I have made a similar recipe with broccoli, and it works just as well with spinach. I used a one pound bag of fresh spinach, microwaved it for 1 1/2 minutes, squeezed out the moisture, then chopped. Omitted the butter. Added a small amount of Andouille sausage, thinly sliced. Reduced the amount of onion and sauteed it with the andouille before adding to the mix.
Really drain spinach extremely well
